# [2610.02571v1] Improving the Energy-Efficiency of the Code Generated by LLMs through Effective Prompting

## Problem
- Despite advances in code generation, frontier LLMs are rarely evaluated based on the energy efficiency of the code they produce. Prior work does not address this — because it only evaluates functional correctness, missing that LLM-generated code can consume up to 450 times more energy than human-written solutions.

## Contribution
- Comprehensive evaluation of 21 prompting strategies for energy-efficient code generation, identifying 8 strategies for evaluation across 10 open-weight and proprietary LLMs.
- Evaluates effectiveness for both Python and C++ code generation relative to a baseline prompt.
- Selected prompting strategies achieved energy reductions of up to 25% for Python and 17% for C++.

## Method (core summary)
- Uses EffiBench dataset: 878 Python-solvable programming problems from LeetCode, 3 difficulty levels (Easy 145, Medium 510, Hard 223), 11 algorithmic categories.
- Extends dataset to C++ by recreating the evaluation framework and analyzing C++ solutions on the AlgoMonster platform.
- Stage 1 (initial analysis): evaluates 110 problems with 22 prompting strategies on 3 models (Kimi K2.7 Code, MiniMax M3, Granite-4.0H-Small), Python only, to identify consistently energy-reducing strategies.
- Filters to 59 problems where all 22 strategies (including baseline) produce functionally correct solutions across all 3 models.
- Stage 2 (extended evaluation): evaluates 8 selected strategies + baseline on 537 Python problems and 607 C++ problems, 10 models.
- Fine-grained energy measurement for Python and C++ programs.

## Key Findings
- 10 models: GPT-5.6 Terra, Claude 4.5 Haiku, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Granite-4.0H-Small, Gemma 4 26B A4B IT, Muse Glimmer 30B, GPT-OSS-120B, Kimi K2.7 Code, MiniMax M3, Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct.
- Selected strategies achieved energy reductions up to 25% for Python and 17% for C++ vs baseline.
- Model level: Python — Granite-4.0-H-Small up to 50%, Claude 4.5 Haiku 39%, MiniMax M3 28%; C++ — Granite-4.0-H-Small up to 56%, Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct 7%.
- Top 8 prompting strategies: Prompt 21 (−49%), 20 (−45%), 12 (−44%), 10 (−39%), 11 (−36%), 13 (−36%), 4 (−35%), 18 (−34%) vs baseline.
- Effectiveness not consistent across models, languages, or strategies — some reduce energy, others increase it vs baseline.
- Strategies require significantly more tokens, increasing inference energy cost — overall efficiency must account for both inference energy and execution energy.

## Actionable Insights
1. Prompting strategy substantially influences energy consumption of LLM-generated code — up to 25% reduction for Python, 17% for C++. Application: experiment with different prompting strategies when generating code for production, measure execution energy not just functional correctness.
2. Prompt strategy effectiveness varies by model and programming language — a strategy reducing energy for Python may increase energy for C++. Application: optimize prompts per model-tier and per language, not one prompt for all cases.

## Assumptions & Limitations
- Evaluation benchmark has imbalanced difficulty distribution (substantially more Medium than Easy or Hard problems).
- Does not encompass full diversity of programming tasks encountered in practice.
- Experiments limited to Python and C++; does not include effects on other programming languages.
- Strategies require more tokens, increasing inference energy cost — overall energy efficiency must account for both inference energy and execution energy.
